title: How to Cancel Audible — Step-by-Step Guide (2026)
metaDescription: Cancel Audible membership and keep your audiobooks. Stop the monthly charge. Get retention offers or pause your account instead.
intro: Audible is hard to cancel by design — Amazon buries the option and throws retention offers at you. But you keep all purchased audiobooks forever, even after canceling. Here's the fastest path.

steps.title: Go to Audible account details
steps.text: Visit audible.com/account/cancel-membership directly. Sign in with your Amazon account if prompted.
steps.tip: Don't try to find this through the Audible app — it's web-only. And Amazon deliberately hides the direct cancel link.

steps.title: Click "Cancel membership"
steps.text: On the cancellation page, click "Cancel membership". Audible will immediately offer alternatives.

steps.title: Decline retention offers
steps.text: Audible will offer: a cheaper plan, a pause (1-3 months), extra credits, or a discount. Click "Continue cancellation" or "No thanks" to proceed past each offer.
steps.tip: If you just need a break, the Pause option (up to 3 months, no charge) is genuinely useful. You keep your credits and renewal date shifts.

steps.title: Select reason and confirm
steps.text: Choose a cancellation reason and click the final "Cancel membership" button. Any unused credits will be forfeited. Downloaded audiobooks remain in your library forever.
steps.tip: USE YOUR REMAINING CREDITS FIRST. Pick any audiobook — credits don't carry over after cancellation.

warnings: Unused credits are forfeited upon cancellation. Spend them on any audiobook before canceling.
You keep ALL audiobooks you've purchased or redeemed with credits — forever. They don't disappear.
The cancellation cannot be done through the Audible mobile app — web only.
Amazon will send multiple 'we miss you' emails with comeback offers after canceling.
If you have an annual plan, unused months/credits are not refunded after the 30-day window.

faqs.q: Do I keep my audiobooks if I cancel Audible?
faqs.a: Yes. All audiobooks you purchased or redeemed with credits are yours forever. You can listen to them anytime through the Audible app, even without a membership.

faqs.q: What happens to my unused Audible credits?
faqs.a: Unused credits are permanently lost when you cancel. Always redeem all credits for audiobooks before canceling — pick anything, even something you might listen to later.

faqs.q: Can I get a refund from Audible?
faqs.a: Within 30 days of renewal, Audible typically offers prorated refunds. After 30 days, refunds are unlikely. Contact customer service for requests.

faqs.q: Can I pause Audible instead of canceling?
faqs.a: Yes. Audible offers a Pause feature for up to 3 months (no charge during pause). You keep your credits and library. Great if you're just catching up on your backlog.

refund.details: Audible offers refunds within 30 days of your most recent charge. After 30 days, refunds are rare. Annual plan members should be especially careful about timing.

retentionTactics: Audible throws 3-4 retention offers at you before allowing cancellation.
Common offers: pause membership (1-3 months), cheaper plan ($7.95/mo for 1 credit every 2 months), free extra credit.
They remind you of unused credits you'll lose.
The cancellation page is intentionally hard to find (not in app, buried on website).
